widgets_values:
# 🎭 Master Guide: Qwen Inpaint Multi-Edit
---
### **🚀 What does this workflow do?** This is a **Spatial Image Editor** powered by the Qwen Inpaint system. It allows you to "stitch" elements from separate images into a single base photo with high accuracy. By using masks, you can tell the AI exactly where to swap clothes, add objects, or change features using external references.
---
### **🛠️ The 4-Step Process** 1️⃣ **Prepare the Base:** Load your main image into the first node. Right-click the image and select **"Open in MaskEditor"** to paint over the specific areas you want to modify.   2️⃣ **Load References:** Use the 2nd and 3rd input nodes to upload your "source" objects (e.g., a specific suit in Image 1, or a bird in Image 2).   3️⃣ **The "Director" Prompt:** Tell the AI exactly what to swap. * *Example:* "Replace the clothes in **image_1** with the suit in **image_2**, then add the bird from **image_3** onto the shoulder."   4️⃣ **Execute:** Hit prompt. Keep your **Seed** on **Fixed** while you refine the mask and the text until the logic is perfect.
---
### **🎛️ Technical Settings: The "Dials"** | Setting | Value | The Impact | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Shift** | **Variable** | **Low:** Sharpens fine textures.
**High:** Handles large-scale structural changes. | | | | | | **Expand** | **10 - 20** | Grows the mask slightly to help the AI blend edges into the original image. | | | | | | **Blur Radius** | **10.0** | Softens the mask edges to avoid a "cut-and-paste" look. |
---
### **💡 Pro Tips for Artists** * **Precision Masking:** You don't need to be a surgeon, but the closer your mask is to the intended shape, the more realistic the final blend will be.   * **Edge Blending:** If the transition looks harsh, bump up the **Blur Radius** slightly to melt the new pixels into the old ones.   * **Reference by Name:** Always use "image_1", "image_2", etc., so the model knows which reference belongs in which masked area.
---

nodes.title: About ImageScaleToMaxDimension
widgets_values: The input image shouldn't be too large (such as more than 3000). A too large input might cause bad results. You can enable the *ImageScaleToMaxDimension* node to download and scale the input image.

nodes.title: About how to create mask
widgets_values:
Right-click on the Load Image node, then click "Open in MaskEditor" to open it and paint the area you want to inpaint.

You can learn more about MaskEditor in the [MaskEditor Document](https://docs.comfy.org/interface/maskeditor)

nodes.title: Note: KSampler settings
widgets_values:
You can test and find the best setting by yourself. The following table is for reference.
| Parameters   | Qwen Team | Comfy Original | with 4steps LoRA |
|--------|---------|------------|---------------------------|
| Steps  | 50      | 20         | 4                         |
| CFG    | 4.0     | 2.5        | 1.0                       |

nodes.title: About ImageCompositeMasked
widgets_values: Some users might want to keep the unmasked area unchanged, though with ImageCompositeMasked, we can paste the original pixels back.

Set cfg to 1.0 for a speed boost at the cost of consistency. Samplers like res_multistep work pretty well at cfg 1.0

The official number of steps is 50 but I think that's too much. Even just 10 steps seems to work.
